 import plotly.express as px
import pandas as pd

data = {
    'Region': [
        'Niamey Urban', 'Niamey Rural', 'Central Plateau East Valley', 'Central Plateau East Highlands',
        'Central Plateau West Valley', 'Central Plateau West Highlands', 'Southern East Irrigated',
        'Southern East Rainfed', 'Southern West Irrigated', 'Southern West Rainfed',
        'Agadez North Remote', 'Agadez North Nearby', 'Agadez South Remote', 'Agadez South Nearby',
        'Dosso Central Irrigated', 'Dosso Central Rainfed', 'Dosso Periphery Irrigated',
        'Dosso Periphery Rainfed', 'Maradi Valley High-Input', 'Maradi Valley Low-Input',
        'Maradi Highlands High-Input', 'Maradi Highlands Low-Input', 'Tillaberi Farmlands Irrigated',
        'Tillaberi Farmlands Rainfed', 'Diffa Irrigation Large', 'Diffa Irrigation Small',
        'Tahoua Savannah Irrigated', 'Tahoua Savannah Rainfed', 'Zinder Agricultural Belt Irrigated',
        'Zinder Agricultural Belt Rainfed', 'Niamey Suburban', 'Dosso South Irrigated',
        'Dosso South Rainfed', 'Zinder North Irrigated', 'Zinder North Rainfed'
    ],
    'Water Productivity (%)': [
        42, 36, 35, 29, 30, 24, 38, 28, 32, 20, 18, 14, 16, 10, 30, 22,
        26, 18, 30, 20, 24, 16, 36, 24, 28, 18, 34, 22, 32, 20, 39, 29,
        23, 35, 25
    ],
    'Season': [
        'Wet', 'Dry', 'Wet', 'Dry', 'Wet', 'Dry', 'Wet', 'Dry',
        'Wet', 'Dry', 'Wet', 'Dry', 'Wet', 'Dry', 'Wet', 'Dry',
        'Wet', 'Dry', 'Wet', 'Dry', 'Wet', 'Dry', 'Wet', 'Dry',
        'Wet', 'Dry', 'Wet', 'Dry', 'Wet', 'Dry', 'Wet', 'Wet',
        'Dry', 'Wet', 'Dry'
    ],
    'Land Area (ha)': [
        1200, 800, 1500, 600, 1100, 400, 2200, 1800, 1900, 1300, 300, 200,
        400, 250, 1000, 900, 800, 700, 1400, 1000, 900, 500, 2100, 1700,
        500, 400, 1800, 1400, 1600, 1200, 950, 1100, 650, 1700, 1300
    ],
    'Farm Size Category': [
        'Large', 'Medium', 'Large', 'Small', 'Large', 'Small', 'Large', 'Medium',
        'Large', 'Small', 'Small', 'Small', 'Small', 'Small', 'Medium', 'Medium',
        'Medium', 'Small', 'Large', 'Medium', 'Medium', 'Small', 'Large', 'Medium',
        'Large', 'Small', 'Large', 'Medium', 'Large', 'Medium', 'Medium', 'Large',
        'Small', 'Large', 'Medium'
    ]
}

df = pd.DataFrame(data)

fig = px.strip(
    df,
    x='Season',
    y='Water Productivity (%)',
    color='Farm Size Category',
    hover_data=['Region', 'Land Area (ha)'],
    category_orders={'Season': ['Wet', 'Dry'], 'Farm Size Category': ['Small', 'Medium', 'Large']},
    color_discrete_sequence=px.colors.qualitative.Plotly,
    title='Water Productivity Across Seasons and Farm Size Categories in Niger',
    labels={'Water Productivity (%)': 'Water Productivity (%)', 'Season': 'Season'},
    height=700,
    width=1000
)

fig.update_layout(
    plot_bgcolor='white',
    xaxis_title='Season',
    yaxis_title='Land Area (ha)',
    legend_title='Farm Size',
    legend=dict(orientation="h", yanchor="bottom", y=1.02, xanchor="right", x=1),
    margin=dict(l=50, r=50, b=50, t=80, pad=10),
    font=dict(size=12)
)

fig.update_traces(
    marker=dict(size=10, opacity=0.7, line=dict(width=1, color='DarkSlateGrey')),
    selector=dict(mode='markers')
)

fig.write_image('output.png')
SUMMARY
 The chart presented is a swarm plot that illustrates water productivity across different seasons and farm size categories in Niger. The title of the chart, located at the top, clearly states this focus: "Water Productivity Across Seasons and Farm Size Categories in Niger." The x-axis represents the two seasons, labeled as "Wet" and "Dry," while the y-axis indicates water productivity as a percentage, ranging from 10% to 45%.

The data points are color-coded based on farm size categories, with a legend at the top right specifying three categories: Small (in teal), Medium (in peach), and Large (in lavender). Each dot on the plot represents a specific data point, showing the water productivity for individual regions during either the wet or dry season, categorized by farm size.

In the wet season, water productivity values show a broader spread, particularly for large farms, which range from approximately 29% to 42%. Medium farms during the wet season exhibit water productivity values mostly between 22% and 36%, while small farms have values primarily between 10% and 30%. In the dry season, the range of water productivity tends to be narrower and generally lower for all farm sizes. Large farms in the dry season exhibit productivity values between 28% and 39%, medium farms range from around 18% to 30%, and small farms have values mostly between 10% and 20%.

Overall, this swarm plot effectively displays the distribution and variation of water productivity across different farm sizes and seasons, highlighting that large farms generally achieve higher water productivity, especially in the wet season.
